instructions: Closed book. For each item: read the stem only and write your solution in stem_only before you read the options. Then choose the answer labels. Use no sources. Set flag to one sentence when you see a second defensible answer or a missing constraint, else null.

items.stem: A company offers an order API from its VPC to 30 business partners in the same AWS Region. Each partner calls the API from its own VPC in its own AWS account. Several partner VPCs use the same CIDR block as the company's VPC. Partners must reach the API privately, and the company must restrict each partner to the API and nothing else in its VPC. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST secure way?

options.label: A
options.text: Put a Network Load Balancer in front of the API, create an endpoint service that allows each partner account, and let each partner create an interface endpoint.

options.label: B
options.text: Create a VPC peering connection with each partner VPC, and allow only the API port from the partner CIDR blocks in the security groups of the API.

options.label: C
options.text: Put a Network Load Balancer in front of the API, create an endpoint service that allows all principals and accepts every request, and publish the service name.

options.label: D
options.text: Share a transit gateway with the partner accounts through AWS RAM, attach every VPC, and give each partner attachment its own transit gateway route table.

items.stem: A company wants to centrally manage routing between three VPCs in one AWS Region. The company creates a transit gateway with default route table association and default route propagation turned on, and attaches the three VPCs. The transit gateway route table now lists the CIDR blocks of all three VPCs. Security groups and network ACLs allow the traffic, but instances in one VPC still cannot reach instances in the other VPCs. What should the company do?

options.label: A
options.text: Turn on appliance mode for each VPC attachment so that the transit gateway keeps each traffic flow in one Availability Zone.

options.label: B
options.text: Add routes for the CIDR blocks of the other VPCs to the subnet route tables of each VPC, with the transit gateway as the target.

options.label: C
options.text: Turn on route propagation from the transit gateway route table to the subnet route tables of each attached VPC.

options.label: D
options.text: Add static routes for the CIDR blocks of the three VPCs to the transit gateway route table, with the VPC attachments as the targets.

items.stem: A company uses a gateway endpoint to restrict access to Amazon S3 from its VPC. The endpoint policy allows s3:GetObject on one bucket for all principals. The bucket is in the same AWS account and has no bucket policy. A new application on Amazon EC2 instances in the VPC gets an access denied error when it reads objects from that bucket. The IAM role in the instance profile has no S3 permissions. What should the company do?

options.label: A
options.text: Change the Principal element of the endpoint policy from all principals to the ARN of the IAM role in the instance profile.

options.label: B
options.text: Add a statement that allows s3:* on the bucket and on its objects to the endpoint policy of the gateway endpoint.

options.label: C
options.text: Replace the gateway endpoint with an interface endpoint for Amazon S3, and attach the same endpoint policy to the new endpoint.

options.label: D
options.text: Attach an identity-based policy that allows s3:GetObject on the objects of the bucket to the IAM role in the instance profile.

items.stem: A company attaches 20 VPCs to one transit gateway that uses its default route table: 10 production VPCs, 9 development VPCs and 1 shared-services VPC. A new security rule says that the company must isolate the production VPCs from the development VPCs. VPCs inside each group must still reach each other, and both groups must still reach the shared-services VPC. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: Create a second transit gateway for the development VPCs, move their attachments to it, and peer the two transit gateways for access to shared services.

options.label: B
options.text: Add network ACL rules that deny traffic from the development CIDR blocks to every subnet in the 10 production VPCs.

options.label: C
options.text: Create one transit gateway route table for each group, associate each attachment with its group's table, and propagate the group's attachments and the shared-services attachment to it.

options.label: D
options.text: Associate the shared-services attachment with a transit gateway route table to which the production and the development attachments both propagate their routes.

options.label: E
options.text: Add inbound rules to the security groups in the production VPCs that deny traffic from the CIDR blocks of the development VPCs.

items.stem: A software as a service (SaaS) company serves customers through an endpoint service. Each customer reaches the service privately through an interface endpoint in its own VPC. One customer's VPC uses the same CIDR block as the company's VPC. A new feature must send status callbacks from the company's VPC to an HTTPS receiver in that customer's VPC. The company must ensure that the callback traffic stays private. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: The customer allows inbound traffic from the company's VPC in the security group of its existing interface endpoint, and the company sends the callbacks back through that endpoint.

options.label: B
options.text: The customer creates an endpoint service for the receiver behind a Network Load Balancer and allows the company's account, and the company creates an interface endpoint to it.

options.label: C
options.text: Both companies attach their VPCs to a transit gateway, and private NAT gateways in each VPC translate the overlapping addresses of the callback traffic.

options.label: D
options.text: The company and the customer create a VPC peering connection between their two VPCs and add routes for the subnet of the receiver in both VPCs.

items.stem: A company runs a shared-services VPC that is peered with two application VPCs in the same AWS Region. Each VPC runs Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets, and the CIDR blocks of the three VPCs do not overlap. The two application VPCs must now also communicate with each other. The company will not add more VPCs. What is the MOST cost-effective solution that meets these requirements?

options.label: A
options.text: Create a transit gateway, attach every VPC to it, and add a route that points to the transit gateway in the route tables of every VPC.

options.label: B
options.text: Add routes in each application VPC that send traffic for the other VPCs through the existing peering connections with the shared-services VPC.

options.label: C
options.text: Create a VPC peering connection between each pair of VPCs that must communicate, and add a route for each peer CIDR block to the route tables.

options.label: D
options.text: Create an endpoint service in each VPC that must be reached, and create an interface endpoint for that service in each VPC that calls it.

items.stem: A company uploads several terabytes of files each month to an Amazon S3 bucket in us-east-1. The company has a VPC in us-east-1. The VPC and the company's data center connect to a transit gateway, and the data center uses an AWS Direct Connect dedicated connection. The files come from Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets of the VPC. The uploads must travel privately and must not pass through an internet gateway. What is the MOST cost-effective solution that meets these requirements?

options.label: A
options.text: Create a gateway endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPC, and associate the endpoint with the route tables of the private subnets of the VPC.

options.label: B
options.text: Create a NAT gateway in each Availability Zone of the VPC, and route the uploads through the NAT gateways to the public endpoint of Amazon S3.

options.label: C
options.text: Create an interface endpoint for Amazon S3 in the private subnets of the VPC, and send the uploads to the endpoint-specific DNS name of the endpoint.

options.label: D
options.text: Create an interface endpoint for Amazon S3 in a new shared-services VPC that is attached to the transit gateway, and send the uploads to that endpoint.

items.stem: A company connects eight spoke VPCs to one hub VPC with VPC peering connections. The hub VPC has NAT gateways in its public subnets. Instances in private subnets of the spoke VPCs must reach the internet for software updates. The company wants to centrally manage outbound internet access in the hub VPC and does not want NAT gateways in the spoke VPCs. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?

options.label: A
options.text: Give the spoke instances Elastic IP addresses, and add a 0.0.0.0/0 route in each spoke VPC that points to the internet gateway of the hub VPC.

options.label: B
options.text: Add a 0.0.0.0/0 route in each spoke VPC that points to its peering connection with the hub VPC, and route the hub subnets to the NAT gateways.

options.label: C
options.text: Run proxy instances behind a Network Load Balancer in the hub VPC, and configure the spoke instances to send their update traffic to the proxy over peering.

options.label: D
options.text: Replace the peering connections with a transit gateway, and route 0.0.0.0/0 from the spoke VPCs through the transit gateway to the NAT gateways in the hub VPC.

items.stem: A company reviews its network costs. NAT gateway data processing is the largest network charge. VPC flow logs, which the company uses to monitor traffic, show that most of the NAT gateway traffic goes to Amazon S3 and Amazon DynamoDB in the same AWS Region. The instances run in private subnets in three Availability Zones, and the design must stay in three Availability Zones. What is the MOST cost-effective way to reduce the charge?

options.label: A
options.text: Send the S3 and DynamoDB traffic through a transit gateway to a central egress VPC that holds shared NAT gateways for the company.

options.label: B
options.text: Move all instances into one Availability Zone, and send all outbound traffic through one NAT gateway in that Availability Zone.

options.label: C
options.text: Create interface endpoints for Amazon S3 and DynamoDB in each Availability Zone, and send the requests to the DNS names of the endpoints.

options.label: D
options.text: Create gateway endpoints for Amazon S3 and DynamoDB, and associate the endpoints with the route tables of the private subnets in each Availability Zone.

items.stem: A company connects 25 VPCs in one AWS Region through a transit gateway. A cost review shows two large charges. One is transit gateway data processing for about 40 TB each month between an analytics VPC and a data VPC. The other is NAT gateway data processing for backups that instances in the data VPC write to Amazon S3 in the same Region. Traffic between the other VPCs is small, and the company must keep the transit gateway for those VPCs. Which combination of steps is the MOST cost-effective way to reduce these charges? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: Create an interface endpoint for Amazon S3 in the data VPC, and send the backups to the endpoint-specific DNS name of the interface endpoint.

options.label: B
options.text: Create a VPC peering connection between the analytics VPC and the data VPC, and route the traffic between the two VPCs over the peering connection.

options.label: C
options.text: Turn on appliance mode for the transit gateway attachments of the analytics VPC and the data VPC to keep each traffic flow in one zone.

options.label: D
options.text: Create a gateway endpoint for Amazon S3 in the data VPC, and associate it with the route tables of the subnets that run the backup jobs.

options.label: E
options.text: Replace the transit gateway with VPC peering connections between all 25 VPCs, and delete the transit gateway attachments of every VPC.

items.stem: A company runs a shared-services VPC that is peered with two application VPCs in the same AWS Region. Each VPC runs Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets, and the CIDR blocks of the three VPCs do not overlap. The company will grow to 150 VPCs, and every VPC must communicate with every other VPC. What is the MOST cost-effective solution that meets these requirements?

options.label: A
options.text: Add routes in each application VPC that send traffic for the other VPCs through the existing peering connections with the shared-services VPC.

options.label: B
options.text: Create a transit gateway, attach every VPC to it, and add a route that points to the transit gateway in the route tables of every VPC.

options.label: C
options.text: Create an endpoint service in each VPC that must be reached, and create an interface endpoint for that service in each VPC that calls it.

options.label: D
options.text: Create a VPC peering connection between each pair of VPCs that must communicate, and add a route for each peer CIDR block to the route tables.

The VPC and the company's data center connect to a transit gateway, and the data center uses an AWS Direct Connect dedicated connection. The files come from on-premises servers in the company's data center. The uploads must travel privately and must not pass through an internet gateway. What is the MOST cost-effective solution that meets these requirements?

options.label: A
options.text: Create an interface endpoint for Amazon S3 in the private subnets of the VPC, and send the uploads to the endpoint-specific DNS name of the endpoint.

options.label: B
options.text: Create an interface endpoint for Amazon S3 in a new shared-services VPC that is attached to the transit gateway, and send the uploads to that endpoint.

options.label: C
options.text: Create a NAT gateway in each Availability Zone of the VPC, and route the uploads through the NAT gateways to the public endpoint of Amazon S3.

options.label: D
options.text: Create a gateway endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPC, and associate the endpoint with the route tables of the private subnets of the VPC.
